changes.after: Show a line of text on the screen.

before: Start here: no coding knowledge is required.
A program is instructions for a computer. A function is a named group of instructions.
package main identifies an executable package. import "fmt" makes the formatting package available in this file. A package groups Go code.
func main() is the entry function. Its braces enclose instructions. fmt.Println("Moon") calls Println from fmt with text; it displays Moon and a newline.

Complete example to read, not an in-app run:
```go
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    fmt.Println("Moon")
}
```

Expected output from this example, explained rather than executed here:
```text
Moon
```
after: You can start here without knowing any code. Code is the written instructions a computer follows.
A program is a set of instructions for a computer. A function is a named group of instructions inside a program.
A package groups Go code. `package main` says this code belongs to a program we can run. `import "fmt"` brings in tools for showing text.
Go starts running our instructions inside `func main()`. The braces `{ }` hold those instructions. `fmt.Println("Moon")` shows the text Moon and then starts a new line.

Follow this example one line at a time.
```go
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    fmt.Println("Moon")
}
```
The screen shows `Moon`. The quotation marks tell Go where the text starts and ends; they do not appear in the result.
